definition: A British colonial territory administered directly by a governor appointed by the British Crown, applied specifically to the Freetown Peninsula from 1808 until independence in 1961.
A territory over which a foreign state exercises sovereignty without formal annexation; proclaimed over the interior hinterland of Sierra Leone by Great Britain in August 1896.

An ethno-linguistic community in Sierra Leone descended from freed African Americans (Nova Scotians), Jamaican Maroons, and Liberated Africans (Recaptives) who developed a distinct Creole language (Krio), culture, and architectural style.
An enslaved person rescued by the British Royal Navy's West Africa Squadron from illegal slave ships post-1807 and resettled in the Sierra Leone Peninsula.
An 1898 armed resistance movement led by Chief Bai Bureh and southern leaders against Governor Cardew's five-shilling annual direct tax on indigenous dwellings.
The recognized traditional ruler and custodian of land in a chiefdom, formalized under colonial indirect rule and maintained in Sierra Leone's local governance system.
An armed rebel movement led by Foday Sankoh that fought against successive Sierra Leonean governments from 1991 to 2002.

Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group, a West African multi-national armed peacekeeping force deployed to restore peace and constitutional order in Sierra Leone during the civil war.
The post-civil war program that successfully disarmed, demobilized, and reintegrated over 75,000 ex-combatants into civilian society between 1998 and 2002.
An independent body established under the 2000 TRC Act and 1999 Lomé Agreement to investigate human rights violations during the civil war and promote national reconciliation.
A hybrid international-national UN-backed tribunal established in Freetown in 2002 to try individuals bearing the greatest responsibility for war crimes and crimes against humanity.
Rough diamonds mined in areas controlled by forces opposed to legitimate governments and sold to fund military conflict.
